data.question: Should we adopt rule change 2 (block_k 2 → 1), which passes the vote but leaves C as the only company against it and has an uncertain gain, or keep the rules at v2 for this period?
data.background: Change 2 raises on_time_deliveries by +1.2 on average, but only 2/5 seeds improve, and only about 4 late deliveries remain to recover (4.2 now). The prior expectation was that this step would fail the 2-of-3 vote and need another override. The measured votes are A ○, B ○, C ×, so it would pass, but C would be outvoted again and its utility would fall from 56.3 to 40.1. In D1 you asked us to re-measure C's utility and the road violations before going further, so the trade-off between a small, uncertain town-wide gain and a large burden on one company is yours to make, not ours.

options.summary: Adopt block_k 2 → 1. On-time deliveries go from 223.8 to 225.0 (+1.2, improved on 2/5 seeds) and late deliveries from 4.2 to 3.0. Blocked time falls from 936 s to 130 s. worst_company_p95_wait_s falls from 109 to 92.4, and the lowest on-time rate rises from 0.97 to 0.98. Road violations rise from 28.0 to 29.8, and C's utility drops from 56.3 to 40.1. Votes are A ○, B ○, C ×, so the change passes 2-of-3 without an override. Check, constitution and KPI conditions all pass.
options.stakeholders: B gains most (utility 65.5 → 74.2) and A is unchanged (73.4). C loses heavily (56.3 → 40.1) and likely faces more sanctions, since road violations rise. Customers of the worst-served company wait less at p95 (109 → 92.4 s), and town-wide about 1 more order per period arrives on time. That customer gain is not reliable across seeds.

options.summary: Stay at v2. On-time deliveries stay at 223.8, late deliveries at 4.2 and worst_company_p95_wait_s at 109. Unfinished stays at 0.0, road violations at 28.0, and utilities stay at 73.4 / 65.5 / 56.3. This leaves time to do the re-measurement of C and road violations that D1 asked for, and to test change 2 on more seeds.
options.stakeholders: C avoids a 16-point utility loss and further sanctions. B gives up a gain of about 8.7 utility. Customers keep the current service: 0.97 lowest on-time rate and a 109 s worst-company p95 wait. Both are already within the 120 s promise, but they forgo a small, uncertain improvement.

recommendation.reason: The main-goal gain is small (+1.2) and not robust (only 2/5 seeds), while the cost to C is large and certain in the measurement (56.3 → 40.1) and road violations rise again (28.0 → 29.8). D1 asked to re-measure C's burden before going further. Current service already meets the promise for most orders (0.97 lowest on-time rate, p95 wait 109 s, 0 unfinished). Re-measuring change 2 on more seeds first gives a sounder basis than adopting it now. If you weigh the worst-company wait reduction (109 → 92.4 s) heavily, option 2 is defensible and passes the vote on its own.

unknowns: Whether the +1.2 gain holds with more than 5 seeds, or is noise.
Why C's utility stands at 56.3 now when D1 recorded 28.8 → 19.0, i.e. whether the utility scale or measurement changed between periods.
How C will respond to repeated losses and being outvoted (e.g. changed routing, more violations, or leaving).
Which sanctions C's added road violations would trigger and what they would cost.
How customers perceive a p95 wait of 109 s versus 92.4 s, given the 120 s promise.
What the KPI means by 'kept waiting badly'; no threshold has been set yet (K1 deferred it).
Next period's demand level and mix across companies, which could change the size of the gain.
Whether intermediate settings or other rules (e.g. hold_limit, mode transitions) could get the wait reduction with less cost to C.
